This Hebrew verb means “longed,” expressing a strong desire for something. As a verb, it describes an action rather than naming a person, place, or object. The word occurs 329 times in the Hebrew Old Testament, showing that fear is a recurring human response addressed throughout those Scriptures.

This Hebrew word refers to a “garment,” an item worn by a person. It functions as a noun naming what someone wears, rather than an action or quality. The precise significance in either passage depends on the surrounding verse and passage.
